title: Hillsborough County Annual Financial Report, fiscal year 2024-2025 (Florida Department of Financial Services form, as filed by the county)

caveats: Compiled from data obtained from the Florida Department of Financial Services, Division of Accounting and Auditing, Bureau of Local Government.

In preparation for the implementation of GASB Statement No. 84, the Department of Financial Services added the Custodial Fund column to the Annual Financial Report in FY 2020-21. Custodial Fund reporting is used to account for assets held by a government in a purely custodial capacity. For example, a county or municipal government might collect taxes or other revenues on behalf of other agencies or local governments, and these transactions would be recorded in the Custodial Fund. Since fiscal years prior to FY 2020-21 did not include Custodial Fund reporting, the account totals for FY 2020-21 and subsequent fiscal years may not be directly comparable.
The workbook "Total Account" column sums every fund column, including fiduciary funds (custodial, pension, trust, private purpose) and Component Units, which are legally separate entities.

Amounts are as reported by the county in its Annual Financial Report; expenditures include inter-fund transfers (account 581), so summing across funds counts money moved between county funds in both the sending and receiving fund.
Account codes are stored as numbers in the workbook, so trailing zeros of Uniform Accounting System codes are not preserved (e.g. 312.30 appears as 312.3).
Per-capita figures in the workbook use the April 1 population estimate for the calendar year in which the fiscal year ends.

FY 2022-23, excluding custodial amounts: expenditure account 581 (inter-fund transfers out, $1,160,934,246) exceeds revenue account 381 (transfers in, $536,330,405) by $624,603,841. Non-custodial figures, FY 2022-23: account 521 $732,874, public safety $387.4M, General Fund 581 $787.4M; compared with FY 2021-22: account 521 $511.3M, public safety $883.3M, General Fund 581 $121.3M; FY 2024-25: account 521 $716.3M, public safety $1.30B, General Fund 581 $341.1M. The county's own Annual Financial Report filed with the Florida CFO (source county-afr-hillsborough-fy2023) shows the same values: expenditure 521 general $203,849 (page 18); expenditure 581 general $787,390,037 (page 22); revenue 381 general $168,326,824 (page 16). Cells: 2023!P124, 2023!P57, 2023!P16, 2023!D16, 2023!D57.

FY 2023-24, excluding custodial amounts: expenditure account 581 (inter-fund transfers out, $1,310,890,615) exceeds revenue account 381 (transfers in, $775,012,474) by $535,878,141. Non-custodial figures, FY 2023-24: account 521 $9.0M, public safety $368.2M, General Fund 581 $912.3M; compared with FY 2021-22: account 521 $511.3M, public safety $883.3M, General Fund 581 $121.3M; FY 2024-25: account 521 $716.3M, public safety $1.30B, General Fund 581 $341.1M. The county's own Annual Financial Report filed with the Florida CFO (source county-afr-hillsborough-fy2024) shows the same values: expenditure 521 general $150,746 (page 8); expenditure 581 general $912,284,168 (page 11); revenue 381 general $186,897,223 (page 7). caveats: Values are April 1 figures. Most years are BEBR estimates published that year; 2000, 2010 and 2020 also have census counts. These are not intercensal-revised series, so a census year can step up or down relative to the estimates around it.
For 2020 the pipeline uses the revised BEBR estimate (the value EDR used for FY 2019-20 per-capita figures); the 2020 census count is listed as an alternate.
EDR notes that countywide figures do not reflect the population estimates ultimately used for revenue-sharing purposes.

Per-resident figures for FY 2009-10 divide by the April 1, 2010 census count (1,229,226); FY 2008-09 used the April 1, 2009 BEBR estimate (1,196,892), a change of 2.7%. These are point-in-time figures from different sources, not a revised continuous series.

Per-resident figures for FY 2020-21 divide by the April 1, 2021 BEBR estimate (1,490,374); FY 2019-20 used the revised April 1, 2020 BEBR estimate (1,478,759), a change of 0.8%. The April 1, 2020 census count was 1,459,762. These are point-in-time figures from different sources, not a revised continuous series.
